source_document.body:
There is a stark difference between the histories of the two companies named 2026 Best Places to Work in the Power Industry. Babcock & Wilcox (B&W) was founded in 1867 by two friends who designed the first inherently safe water-tube boiler. BrilliT is an information technology (IT) firm formed in 2022 inside an electric cooperative. B&W has about 1,650 employees worldwide, although it entered through its Akron, Ohio, headquarters, which had 471 employees at the time of the survey. BrilliT, which also won in 2025, has 31. Both are recognized for reasons that overlap more than their background and size might suggest.
Now in its third year, the program, conducted with Best Companies Group (BCG), recognizes employers based on employee surveys and a detailed look at workplace policies. The submissions B&W and BrilliT provided to BCG describe workplaces where pay, time off, and a clear path for advancement form the foundation. B&W builds on that foundation with flexible scheduling, regular access to senior leaders, and a long list of programs designed to make the workday more enjoyable.
To be eligible, power companies and the vendors that serve them must have at least 15 full- or part-time employees in the U.S. or Canada and have been in business for at least a year. Organizations may enter as a single location, in which case the location appears in their name on the list. B&W entered as “The Babcock & Wilcox Company (Akron, Ohio Headquarters).” B&W said the programs described below are offered across the U.S. and Canada and at many of its international locations.
Participants complete two parts, and both are required. Employers answer a questionnaire about policies, practices, and demographics. Employees take an online engagement and satisfaction survey of roughly 77 statements, plus several open-ended and demographic questions. BCG then analyzes the data and ranks the participating organizations. The descriptions quoted below come from the winners’ submissions to BCG.
Pay, Advancement, and Time Off
BrilliT, a wholly owned subsidiary of Rappahannock Electric Cooperative (REC), manages the IT infrastructure, networking, and security for all of the cooperative’s technology assets. REC is a member-owned utility serving more than 185,000 connections in portions of 22 counties in Virginia. BrilliT said its employees would point first to pay and benefits and to opportunities for promotion. Among its less common offerings, the company listed tuition reimbursement and a generous vacation and sick leave policy.
BrilliT’s winner profile stresses its familiarity with its utility customer. “We know first-hand what keeps electric utility leaders and employees up at night,” the company said, adding that “our clients need a partner as invested as they are in their company, community, and future.” Its leadership has decades of combined experience in both the energy and IT industries. “Our networks are full of smart, dedicated people,” BrilliT said.
B&W’s list is similar on the fundamentals. The company cited competitive compensation, bonuses, a 401(k), flexible health plan options, and career development “with a focus on promoting from within.” It also pointed to incentive and recognition programs “to help reinforce to employees they are valued and valuable contributors to our company.” On time off, B&W said it offers generous vacation, including a paid end-of-year shutdown from Christmas through New Year’s Day, though some areas follow alternate schedules to maintain service.
Flexibility, Culture, and Perks
Where B&W goes further is in how, and where, employees do their work. Its Responsible and Flexible Workplace Program, known as ReFlex, gives employees flexibility in their work hours. Employees also choose their work location, with the option of working 100% remotely, in the office, or in a hybrid arrangement. B&W put both of those programs among the top three things its employees would say they love.
The company also invests heavily in making sure employees know where the business is headed. B&W’s communication programs include an intranet updated daily, quarterly all-employee addresses by senior leadership, and an Executive Lunch Program in which senior leaders meet monthly with a group of employees in a casual setting. A separate question and answer program lets employees submit questions electronically and receive answers from the appropriate decision maker.
B&W’s other programs are meant to build camaraderie. Free lunches, donut and ice cream socials, and raffles for tickets to sporting events are common. The workplace includes a ping-pong table and golf simulator, with an arcade game on the way, and team wins are celebrated with free popcorn, donuts, or other snacks.
Its Children’s Holiday Program is more unusual. Employees’ children through age 11 receive a customized letter from Santa that includes input from their parent about the child’s interests, accomplishments, and gift wishes, along with a $25 gift card. B&W also coordinates volunteer activities on company time, including Earth Day cleanups, Food Bank volunteering, Adopt-a-Family, and the United Way “Day of Caring.”
For all of its programs, B&W’s most telling claim is about longevity. “Our employees consistently tell us that B&W is a place where they can build an entire career,” the company said, noting that it has “quite a few ‘generational employees’ whose grandparents and parents have also worked for our company.” B&W said its success is rooted in teamwork, “a value dating to its earliest days.”
Plenty of employers now offer flexible schedules and free lunches. Fewer can say that a family keeps coming back to the same employer, and that may be the strongest evidence of a good workplace in either company’s submission.
—Aaron Larson is POWER’s executive editor.
